title: Gold Price Surges 3% Above $4,040 as US Dollar Falls Following Midterm Elections
body: Key takeaways Gold jumps 3% after Democrats win Congress Dollar hits one-month low as Treasury yields decline Fed rate expectations remain a risk for bullion Gold prices surged above $4,040 per ounce on November 4, gaining approximately 3% as the US dollar weakened sharply following Democratic victories in the midterm elections. The reversal also marks a sharp change from the previous gold market selloff , when rising interest-rate expectations and technology-stock losses pressured precious metals. Gold Rallies as Dollar Hits One-Month Low The immediate catalyst was the US midterm election outcome, which saw Democrats secure control of both the House of Representatives and Senate. Investors responded by selling dollars and purchasing Treasury bonds as they reassessed fiscal policy, technology regulation and the possibility of congressional gridlock. The US dollar index fell approximately 0.6% to 101.27, its lowest level in a month, while the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield dropped nearly five basis points to around 4.915%. Both developments supported gold. Because bullion is priced internationally in dollars, a weaker greenback makes it less expensive for buyers using other currencies. Lower bond yields also reduce the opportunity cost of holding an asset that pays no interest. This relationship previously supported gold during an August rally above $4,500 . Hamad Hussain, senior economist at Capital Economics, told Reuters that the Democratic sweep appeared to increase investor concerns about the US fiscal outlook, contributing to demand for precious metals. However, the election's economic consequences remain uncertain, and Congress cannot independently determine Federal Reserve policy. Silver and Precious Metals Join the Rally Gold was not the only precious metal benefiting from Wednesday's market reaction. Spot silver climbed approximately 4.8% to $52.13 per ounce, while platinum gained 3.6% to $1,467.60 and palladium advanced 6.5% to $995.06. The broad gains suggest investors were responding to currency movements and shifting macroeconomic expectations rather than a gold-specific catalyst. Earlier gold price analysis highlighted how changes in Federal Reserve expectations can influence precious metals even when underlying demand remains strong. Gold's recovery also follows a period when central-bank purchases failed to prevent declines , illustrating the importance of financial conditions for short-term pricing. Can Gold Hold Above $4,000? Despite Wednesday's rally, investors remain cautious about the Federal Reserve's next interest-rate decision. Markets were pricing an approximately 82% probability of a December rate increase, according to Reuters. Higher rates could strengthen the dollar and increase the relative appeal of interest-bearing assets. Attention now turns to Friday's US nonfarm payrolls report, which could reshape expectations for the Fed's policy path. An earlier weaker-than-expected jobs report demonstrated how quickly bullion can respond when Treasury yields decline. Goldman Sachs also recently lowered its year-end gold forecast to $4,650, while retaining a longer-term constructive outlook.

title: Bitbase Launches ORIGIN, a Points Season That Rewards Consistency
body: PANAMA CITY, November 4, 2026 — Bitbase today launched ORIGIN, the first season of its Bitbase Points program, which is designed to reward sustained participation over time. Over the 26-week season, which ends on May 4, 2027, Bitbase will distribute 1,000,000 points each week, allocated daily according to each participant’s contribution. Four sources of contribution Each participant’s contribution is drawn from four sources: trading, assets held on Bitbase, consistent activity and referrals. Consistent activity is counted as a separate source, so continued participation from day to day adds to a user’s contribution. All eligible users, whether new to Bitbase or already active on the platform, are enrolled automatically. For each new user referred directly, the referrer receives an additional 25% of that user’s contribution. The new user’s own points are not affected. Participants will also receive a Trading Identity card, a shareable summary of their trading style. The first cards will be issued on November 9, with new cards following each Monday for the remainder of the season. Existing users begin with points already credited Before the season began, Bitbase credited points to eligible existing users based on their earlier activity on the platform. As a result, these users enter ORIGIN with their prior activity already reflected in their points and ranking. The first program under Bitbase 2.0 On November 2, the exchange introduced Bitbase 2.0 , updating its brand, app and website under the statement “Market Flows. We Focus.” ORIGIN is the first program to put that statement into practice. While markets move continuously, Bitbase has chosen to assess participation across months rather than individual moments. “We designed ORIGIN for users who participate consistently, not only during the busiest periods in the market,” said Nicholas Lo, Chief Business Officer at Bitbase. “Over a six-month season, that consistency carries weight. Our responsibility is to make sure every contribution is credited, from the first day of the season to the last.” Points and rankings are available in the Bitbase app and at bitbase.com/points. Bitbase aims to give users a stable and straightforward trading experience, in line with its brand statement, “Market Flows. We Focus.” Learn more at bitbase.com. title: Stock Market Today: Dow, Nasdaq and S&P 500 Rebound After Democratic Midterm Election Sweep
body: Key takeaways Dow futures jump as Democrats capture both congressional chambers AMD rallies after data-center revenue nearly doubles Tesla and AI infrastructure stocks face election-related pressure US stock futures rallied Wednesday, November 4, after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, reversing overnight losses as investors reassessed the implications for economic policy and technology regulation. Dow Jones futures surged 1.44%, S&P 500 futures gained 1.04%, and Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.93% by 6:24 a.m. ET. The rebound follows Tuesday's cautious market positioning , when investors weighed election uncertainty and weakening confidence in artificial intelligence stocks. Dow and Nasdaq Futures Reverse Losses After US Midterms Wall Street initially reacted negatively to the Democratic sweep, with Nasdaq-100 futures dropping as much as 2.4% overnight and S&P 500 futures losing approximately 1.4%. However, those losses reversed as investors considered whether divided government could limit sweeping legislative changes during the remainder of President Donald Trump's term. Democrats secured control of both the House and Senate, potentially increasing congressional oversight of technology companies, fiscal policy and cryptocurrency regulation. The recovery was accompanied by a weaker US dollar and declining Treasury yields. The benchmark 10-year yield fell toward 4.92%, reversing some of the pressure described in Coinpaper's recent Treasury market analysis . Meanwhile, October private-sector payrolls increased by 86,000, according to ADP, exceeding economists' expectations of approximately 69,000. The report offered another indication of labor-market resilience ahead of Friday's official employment figures. AMD Stock Surges as AI Chip Revenue Jumps 97% Advanced Micro Devices emerged as one of Wednesday's notable gainers, climbing approximately 6.3% in premarket trading after reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly results. According to AMD's official earnings release , third-quarter revenue reached $13.38 billion, increasing 45% year over year. Data-center revenue surged 97% to $8.55 billion, driven by demand for EPYC processors and Instinct AI accelerators. AMD also forecast approximately $17 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and indicated that growth could accelerate in 2027. The results provide fresh evidence of strong AI infrastructure demand, supporting the investment thesis behind earlier AMD stock forecasts . Other technology shares also advanced. Amazon gained approximately 3%, while Nvidia, Meta and Alphabet climbed more than 1% in early trading. Nevertheless, the rebound follows a severe Nasdaq-100 correction , which recently pushed the index more than 10% below its October high. Tesla Falls While Solar Stocks Rally Not all companies participated in Wednesday's recovery. Tesla and SpaceX shares declined more than 4% in early trading as investors assessed potential regulatory changes and greater congressional scrutiny. Meanwhile, IREN, Hut 8 and Applied Digital weakened amid concerns that newly elected officials could restrict data-center construction in states including Texas and Georgia. Those concerns add to the pressure already highlighted during the recent AI stock selloff . Renewable-energy shares moved in the opposite direction, with First Solar rising 8.3% and Canadian Solar gaining 8.9% in premarket trading. The divergence suggests investors are reassessing which industries could benefit from changes in energy and technology policy. For Wall Street, the next test will be whether the broad market recovery can continue beyond the opening bell. Investors are also monitoring Nvidia's international AI business and upcoming corporate earnings for clues about the durability of technology spending.

title: XRP approaches $1.30 amid US election-driven crypto recovery
body: XRP is surging higher toward $1.30 on Wednesday as improving cryptocurrency market sentiment and increased whale withdrawals from exchanges provide support for the token's recovery. The rebound comes amid developments surrounding the US midterm elections, with the Democratic Party securing a Senate victory and moving toward broader congressional control, according to the reported election results. Bitcoin has also recovered above $78,000 after falling toward a six-week low near $76,000 following the $6.3 billion Binance security breach. The broader recovery appears to be encouraging renewed interest in XRP, while on-chain data suggests that large holders have been moving substantial amounts of the cryptocurrency away from centralized exchanges. However, despite the improving sentiment, XRP continues to trade below several important technical resistance levels, leaving the sustainability of the rebound uncertain. XRP whale withdrawals rise 74.5% as exchange supply declines Large XRP holders have significantly increased their withdrawals from cryptocurrency exchanges over the past week. According to CryptoQuant data, cumulative whale net outflows across multiple exchanges reached approximately 696 million XRP on Wednesday. That compares with 399 million XRP on October 28, representing a 74.5% increase over seven days. The rise suggests that large holders have been withdrawing more XRP from exchanges, potentially reducing the amount immediately available for spot trading. Additional CryptoQuant data points to a notable change in the balance between large and smaller XRP market participants. The XRP Whale vs Retail Spread on Binance climbed to 98.4% on Tuesday, reaching its highest reading since October 15, 2024. By comparison, the corresponding reading across centralized exchanges stood at 65.1%. The difference suggests that whale-related activity on Binance has become particularly pronounced relative to retail activity. For XRP to establish a more convincing bullish trend, the improvement in on-chain metrics would need to be accompanied by stronger spot demand and a breakout above major technical resistance levels. US midterm elections support broader cryptocurrency recovery XRP's rebound comes alongside a broader recovery across the cryptocurrency market. The reported Democratic victory in the US Senate and expectations of further congressional gains have coincided with improving sentiment toward digital assets. Bitcoin has reclaimed the $78,000 level after last week's Binance-related sell-off pushed prices toward $76,000. The recovery suggests that some of the immediate uncertainty surrounding the security breach has begun to ease. Other factors, including the US dollar's performance, liquidity conditions, and investor positioning, may also be contributing to the rebound. XRP faces resistance at $1.30 and $1.34 Despite its recent gains, XRP's daily chart continues to show a cautious technical structure. The token is trading above $1.28 but remains below its major Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs), indicating that the broader corrective phase has not yet ended. Immediate resistance lies near $1.30, where the middle boundary of the Bollinger Bands is positioned. Above $1.30, the next resistance emerges at the 100-day EMA around $1.32. The 50-day EMA at $1.34 represents another significant hurdle. These moving averages form a concentrated resistance area that buyers must overcome to strengthen the bullish outlook. A decisive daily close above $1.34 would suggest that XRP is beginning to regain control of its short- and medium-term trend. However, until XRP reclaims these levels, rallies remain vulnerable to renewed selling pressure. Momentum indicators suggest that XRP's selling pressure is beginning to weaken, although buyers have not yet established a clear advantage. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is hovering around 43, slightly below the neutral level of 50. A sustained move above 50 would provide additional evidence that buyers are gaining influence over short-term price movements. Meanwhile, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicator has turned slightly positive. The improvement suggests that downside momentum may be fading and that a recovery attempt is developing. On the downside, the lower Bollinger Band near $1.23 represents the next meaningful support level. If XRP fails to hold its recent gains and breaks below $1.23, bearish momentum could strengthen again, increasing the risk of further losses. For now, XRP's near-term outlook depends on whether rising whale withdrawals and improving market sentiment can generate enough buying pressure to overcome the $1.30–$1.34 resistance zone. title: Hong Kong Passes Crypto Reporting Bill, CARF Starts In 2027
body: Hong Kong’s Legislative Council has passed legislation adopting the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), setting out new information-collection duties for crypto service providers from January 2027. The government confirmed the bill’s passage on November 4. Under the framework, businesses that fall within its scope will have to identify customers, establish their tax residency and report specified crypto transactions to the Inland Revenue Department (IRD). Hong Kong plans to begin exchanging the information with participating jurisdictions in 2028. The same legislation also updates the Common Reporting Standard (CRS), which covers financial account information and will include additional digital financial products. The changes concern tax reporting and information exchange; they do not introduce a blanket tax on crypto holdings or prohibit people from trading digital assets. Hong Kong’s CARF Rules Set Reporting Duties For Crypto Service Providers The legislation brings Hong Kong into line with the OECD’s CARF, a framework published in 2023 to give tax authorities a standard way to exchange information about crypto-asset transactions across borders. The rules apply to reporting crypto-asset service providers with a relevant connection to Hong Kong. That can include businesses incorporated or organised in the city, entities managed there, tax-resident providers and businesses with a regular place of business or branch in Hong Kong. The scope depends on the services a business provides, rather than whether it calls itself an exchange. The IRD lists crypto exchanges, brokers, dealers and certain crypto-asset ATM operators among the examples. A provider can be covered when it carries out or facilitates exchanges between crypto-assets, or between crypto-assets and traditional currencies, for customers. Hong Kong Passes Crypto Tax Reporting Law, With Data Collection Starting in 2027 Hong Kong’s Legislative Council passed the Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and Amended Common Reporting Standard) Bill 2026 on November 4, implementing the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Under the new law, relevant crypto-asset service providers will be required to collect transaction information starting in 2027, with Hong Kong beginning automatic exchanges of crypto-related tax information with partner jurisdictions in 2028. The amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) will take effect in 2028, with automatic exchanges of financial account information under the updated standard beginning in 2029. Hong Kong’s Financial Services and the Treasury Secretary Christopher Hui said the legislation aims to strengthen international tax transparency and combat cross-border tax evasion. — Wu Blockchain (@WuBlockchain) November 4, 2026 From January 1, 2027, covered providers will have to carry out due diligence on customers and collect information needed to establish their tax residency. For individuals, this includes their name, address, tax-residence jurisdiction and taxpayer identification number. For companies and other entities, providers may also need information about the people who control them. The IRD says new customers will be asked to provide tax-residency self-certifications, while existing customers will have to complete the process within 12 months after the rules take effect . Businesses will also need to register with the department, file annual returns and keep records supporting their checks and reports. The department plans to issue guidance and provide technical support as companies prepare for the requirements. Hong Kong Plans First Crypto Tax Information Exchanges In 2028 Hong Kong’s new reporting rules will also make it easier for tax authorities in other countries to check crypto activity involving their residents. Once the information-sharing system begins in 2028, participating jurisdictions will be able to receive details about reportable crypto transactions involving their tax residents. Whether those transactions are taxable will still depend on the laws of each country. The bill also changes Hong Kong’s existing Common Reporting Standard (CRS), which has been used to exchange financial account information with other jurisdictions since 2018. The revised rules will take effect in January 2028 and cover additional products, including central bank digital currencies, certain electronic money products and derivatives linked to crypto-assets. Financial institutions will also have to collect some additional details about account holders and the people who control those accounts. The first information exchanges under the updated CRS are expected in 2029. The two frameworks therefore have separate timelines: crypto service providers begin CARF due diligence and collection in 2027, with cross-border exchanges planned for 2028. The amended CRS takes effect in 2028, with exchanges following in 2029. The IRD says it will publish further guidance for affected businesses. For crypto users, the immediate change is that covered platforms will ask for tax-residency information and maintain records for reporting purposes. The legislation does not mean every wallet or every transaction is directly reported to overseas authorities.

title: Top XRPL Validator Explains the Difference Between XRP and RLUSD
body: The XRP Ledger supports multiple assets with distinct functions, but XRP and RLUSD occupy fundamentally different positions within its ecosystem. XRPL Validator Vet has outlined the differences between the two assets, explaining how their design, level of control, and intended uses separate them beyond their price characteristics. RLUSD is a dollar backed stablecoin issued by Ripple. As its issuer, Ripple operates under US regulations and retains the ability to freeze RLUSD. XRP, however, has no central issuer or jurisdiction governing it. No single entity can freeze the asset. Vet described XRP simply as a commodity . What's the difference between XRP and stablecoins like RLUSD? RLUSD is optional. XRP isn't. RLUSD is a dollar-backed token issued by Ripple. As the issuer, Ripple has to follow US law and can freeze RLUSD. XRP has no issuer and no jurisdiction, and nobody can freeze it. It's a… — Vet (@Vet_X0) November 3, 2026 How the Ledger Treats Each Asset XRP holds a unique position within the XRP Ledger’s structure. Every account requires an XRP reserve, while transaction fees are paid exclusively in XRP. RLUSD operates differently because users must establish a trust line before they can hold the stablecoin. The decentralized exchange also gives XRP a distinct function. When users execute cross currency swaps, the XRPL automatically evaluates whether routing the transaction through XRP would provide a better exchange rate. For example, when exchanging USD for EUR, the system can assess XRP as an intermediary asset to determine whether it offers a more efficient route. This feature gives XRP a role in the ledger’s liquidity infrastructure that other issued assets do not automatically receive. Volatility and Different Use Cases Vet also explained why XRP’s price volatility serves a different purpose from RLUSD’s stability. XRP has no backing asset determining its market price. Instead, its value fluctuates according to market demand and trading activity. Vet described this volatility as “exactly what attracts traders and investors.” RLUSD serves a different audience by maintaining a value equivalent to $1. This makes it suitable for payroll, invoices, and other financial operations where price fluctuations could create uncertainty. For transactions requiring a neutral asset outside the control of any government or central issuer, Vet considers XRP the appropriate option. He described it as “the only choice on the XRP Ledger” for this particular purpose. He also explained the advantage for market makers. Using XRP to connect liquidity pools allows them to manage exposure to a single asset without taking on the additional counterparty risks associated with an individual token issuer. Debate Over Demand for Native Assets Another commenter, Frank, acknowledged the differences Vet described but questioned how they translate into XRP’s market value. Frank noted that XRP’s valuation depends on its monetary premium, making demand from holders a more relevant measure than transaction volume or token burns alone. Vet responded by referencing the performance of native assets across the cryptocurrency market. “Native assets make up the majority of the total market cap of crypto,” he wrote, adding that demand for this asset category had increased. Could XRP Support Institutional Settlement? The discussion also covered whether institutions such as DTCC and Euroclear could use XRP for settlement. One commenter said clarity on this possibility would be important to retail holders. Vet explained that institutions can use the XRP Ledger whenever they choose, without requiring permission from a central authority. “If the DTCC wants to use the XRP Ledger they can do that. Whenever they want to. They don’t need to ask for permission,” he stated. His response reflects the ledger’s open access structure, which allows institutions to determine independently whether its infrastructure meets their settlement requirements. title: Circle Cuts 5% of Workforce as CRCL Stock Reacts to $865 Million Earnings Report
body: Key takeaways Circle eliminated approximately 5% of its workforce Restructuring costs reached $9.1 million despite higher profits CRCL investors weigh strong earnings against declining reserve income Circle Internet Group , the company behind the USDC stablecoin , disclosed that it cut approximately 5% of its workforce during the third quarter of 2026, even as revenue climbed and quarterly profit exceeded Wall Street expectations. According to Circle's November 4 earnings release , the restructuring generated $9.1 million in expenses, primarily covering employee severance, notice periods, benefits and related costs. Circle Cuts Jobs Despite $226 Million Quarterly Profit Circle said the workforce reduction was designed to align its organizational structure with its operating model and strategic priorities. The company did not disclose the exact number of affected employees. Based on approximately 1,100 workers reported at the end of 2025, a 5% reduction would represent roughly 55 positions, although the actual figure depends on staffing levels when the cuts occurred. The restructuring coincided with substantially stronger headline financial results. Circle reported $865 million in third-quarter revenue and reserve income, up 17% year over year, while net income increased 5% to $226 million. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 85% to $317 million, reflecting lower distribution costs and revenue associated with its Arc blockchain. However, the earnings increase masks an important change in Circle's underlying business. Reserve income, generated primarily from assets backing USDC, declined 8% to $658 million as the company's reserve return rate fell to 3.5%. Meanwhile, other revenue surged to $207 million, including $182 million recognized from an ARC token presale. That distinction matters because the token sale provided a substantial one-time boost rather than recurring interest income. Earlier analysis of Circle's revenue model highlighted how distribution expenses and interest rates affect profitability even when stablecoin usage expands. CRCL Stock Reacts as USDC Growth Slows CRCL shares closed November 3 at $75.22, gaining approximately 4.36% during the session. The stock subsequently attracted premarket buying following Wednesday's earnings announcement, although early trading remained volatile. Investors are evaluating whether Circle's expanding financial infrastructure can compensate for weaker returns on stablecoin reserves. Average USDC circulation increased 8% to $73.3 billion, but the quarter-end supply remained essentially unchanged year over year at $73.9 billion. Meanwhile, USDC's market share declined to 27%, down approximately 1.83 percentage points. The slowdown contrasts with Circle's earlier regulatory expansion , which helped strengthen its position in the institutional stablecoin market. The company also continues expanding distribution through a $100 million Binance investment and a five-year commercial partnership. Can Circle's Arc Blockchain Support CRCL Stock? Circle is attempting to reduce its dependence on reserve income through payments infrastructure, blockchain services and tokenized financial applications. Its Arc blockchain launch attracted more than 100 institutional and ecosystem builders, while Circle Payments Network reached $41.3 billion in annualized transaction volume. The company also plans to acquire Singapore-based payments provider Tazapay, subject to regulatory approval. However, Arc's early revenue contribution does not establish that the business can repeatedly generate similar token-sale proceeds. The distinction is particularly relevant as ARK Invest recently purchased Circle shares during the broader cryptocurrency market correction.

title: Judge orders Bitcoin laptop returned to killer William Sandeson
body: A Nova Scotia judge has ordered a laptop holding convicted killer William Sandeson’s Bitcoin wallet returned to his family. The judge found that prosecutors did not prove the Bitcoin was linked to the 2015 murder of Taylor Samson. Why would a judge order a killer’s Bitcoin to be returned? Justice John Bodurtha decided on Tuesday in Halifax Supreme Court to return convicted killer William Sandeson’s Bitcoin wallet to his family. Sandeson is currently serving a life sentence in a Quebec prison and took part in the hearing by video. The judge said the Crown had to prove a link between the Bitcoin and the crime, and it did not. He said that the idea that Sandeson would use the Bitcoin in the drug deal was “hypothetical” and there was no proof that Sandeson meant to use it or any proof that he used it in connection with the murder. The laptop which holds the wallet will be given back to Sandeson’s family, but the $5,000 in cash found in his apartment will not be returned, because the judge ruled it was “offence-related property.” Police found the cash hidden at the bottom of a garbage can. At trial, Sandeson testified that he used a $200,000 line of credit to buy drugs. His mother co-signed the credit line, which was meant to pay for university. It still had an $80,000 balance when he was arrested. The value of the wallet is disputed. Sandeson has said it is worth $8,000 to $10,000, while a lawyer for Samson’s family has said it could be worth more than $200,000 today. Bitcoin (BTC) traded at about $78,563 on CoinMarketCap at the time of writing. In a 2024 decision, Justice Cindy Bourgeois of the Nova Scotia Court of Appeal found that Sandeson had about $640,000 in Bitcoin and cash when he was jailed. That decision denied him free legal help for his appeal. How did Sandeson end up in prison? Back in August 2015, Sandeson and Samson were both students at Dalhousie University. Sandeson, who was days away from starting medical school, set up a meeting at his Halifax apartment for what was meant to be a cannabis deal of more than 18 kilograms. He shot Samson, kept the drugs and money, and dumped the body in the Bay of Fundy. Samson’s remains have never been found. Sandeson was first found guilty of first-degree murder, but that verdict was overturned on appeal. At a retrial in 2023, a jury found him guilty of second-degree murder. He admitted to the shooting but said it was self-defense. Samson’s family has fought to keep the laptop locked away, and in December 2022, a court granted a temporary order blocking its return. Samson’s mother, Linda Boutilier, and his brother, Connor Samson, had started a wrongful death lawsuit. Their lawyer, James Goodwin, argued that the Bitcoin could be used to pay them damages if they won. Sandeson restarted the fight in April, when he filed a motion asking for his seized property back. The Crown then applied to keep the cash and laptop, saying they were tainted by crime. Boutilier has attended every court appearance in the case and was in the room for Tuesday’s ruling, though she declined to comment. UK and US courts are also legislating their own versions of custody battles over crypto linked to crime, with over 61,000 BTC tied to Qian Zhimin in the UK and an American prisoner’s failed claim to $345 million in lost Bitcoin. title: LIVE: Wall Street crashes and rebounds after Democrats snatch US House and Senate in historic midterms election
body: Democrats have won control of both the House and Senate, alongside major gubernatorial victories, including Texas. Trump has accepted the election results and says Republicans will work with Democrats, despite tensions over tariffs and the Iran war. Dow futures surged 912 points, or 1.75%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.8%. Nasdaq-100 futures lagged as AI stocks weakened. Crypto stocks are mixed. Coinbase jumped 5.53%, Circle 4.36%, Strategy 3.72%, and Robinhood 2.19%, while Block, PayPal, and MercadoLibre fell.
